sections.title: Purpose of Creation & Ma'rifah
sections.summary: We were created to worship and know Allah; ma'rifah elevates worship from form to presence (ihsan).
bullets: “I did not create jinn and humankind except to worship Me” (Q 51:56) — worship entails knowing, loving, obeying.
Ma'rifah (knowing Allah) is the heart’s light that turns ritual into conscious devotion (ihsan).
The Names guide orientation: Who is the One I face, love, fear, hope for?
True knowledge births humility, gratitude, and service.
Teleology: The human fitrah seeks meaning beyond self; ma'rifah fulfills that trajectory.
questions: What intention do I bring to today’s worship?
Which Name will I live by in the next 24 hours?

sections.title: Sources of Knowing Allah
sections.summary: Revelation anchors knowledge; the Prophetic life embodies it; creation and reason corroborate it.
bullets: Qur'an: explicit Names and implicit signs (ayat) in self and cosmos (Q 41:53).
Sunnah: Prophetic mercy, justice, balance embody the Names.
Creation: order, beauty, contingency mirror Divine attributes.
Reason: operates within revealed guidance; guards from fancy and superstition.
Scholarly tradition: tafsir, hadith, kalam, tasawwuf as complementary lenses.
refs: Q 41:53; Q 59:22–24 (Names); Sahih hadith on ihsan (Jibril).
Al-Ghazali, Ihya’ ‘Ulum al-Din; Ibn al-Qayyim; al-Nawawi.

sections.title: The Beautiful Names (Asma’ al-Husna)
sections.summary: The Names are portals of guidance; they are known without likening Allah to creation and without negation.
bullets: Affirmation without anthropomorphism (tashbih) and transcendence without negation (ta‘til).
Names cluster: Mercy (Rahman/Rahim), Knowledge (Alim/Khabeer), Power (Qadir/Qahhar), Beauty & Majesty (Jamal/Jalal).
Living the Names = aligning intention, action, and character with Divine guidance.
Balance: hope (raja’) with fear (khawf), love (mahabbah) with awe (haybah).
Guarding creed (aqidah) ensures spiritual safety while tasting proximity.
questions: Which Name do I under-live or overemphasize?

sections.title: Classical Arguments for God
sections.summary: Rational signs point to a Necessary Being of perfect attributes; proofs serve awakening, not pride.
bullets: Kalam cosmological: begun universe ⇒ transcendent cause.
Contingency: contingent beings require a Necessary Existent.
Teleology: order, fitness-for-life, intelligibility suggest wisdom.
Moral: objective values fit best within a perfectly just source.
Use proofs as pointers that steady the heart alongside revelation.

sections.title: Science, Cosmology, and Awe
sections.summary: Modern science widens tafakkur horizons without replacing revelation; awe nurtures gratitude and stewardship.
bullets: Fine-tuning discourse: delicate constants compatible with life.
Complexity/Information: emergence invites humility before wisdom.
Quantum limits to naïve reductionism; epistemic modesty matters.
Awe states correlate with pro-sociality and ethical restraint.
Science as ayah-reading: stewardship (khilafah) and trust (amanah).

sections.title: Map of Gaflah (Heedlessness)
sections.summary: Gaflah arises from ego (nafs), appetites (hawa), heedless environments, and attention capture.
bullets: Roots: self-exaltation, desires, chronic distraction, despair.
Manifestations: ritual without heart, delay of repentance, moral numbness, cynicism.
Digital heedlessness: slot-machine feeds, novelty loops, dopamine drift.
Social vectors: consumerism, status games, performative piety (riya’).
Early warnings: sleep of heart, neglect of du‘a, loss of shame (haya’).
questions: Which inputs numb my heart daily?

sections.title: Awakening Cycle: Tawbah → Telafi → Istikrar → Hizmet
sections.summary: A practical loop for renewal: Awareness, Repentance, Repair, Consistency, and Service.
bullets: Farkındalık: name it; don’t rationalize it.
Tawbah: regret + abandonment + resolve + where possible restitution.
Telafi (Repair): counter-acts (sadaka, extra prayer, fasting).
Istikrar (Consistency): small daily deeds loved by Allah.
Hizmet (Service): share benefit; light expands when given.
practices: Immediate two-rak‘ah tawbah prayer after lapses.
Pair each slip with a concrete charity or help task within 24h.

sections.title: Habit Science & Nafs Training
sections.summary: Design environments and routines that make obedience easy and disobedience hard.
bullets: Cue → Routine → Reward: attach dhikr/recitation to stable cues (after salat, commutes).
Friction engineering: block, filter, schedule; remove triggers; add delays.
Replacement > suppression: swap with halal, meaningful activities.
Streak psychology: guard first 7, 30, 90 days with shields and allies.
Relapse math: treat a lapse as data; re-enter the cycle fast.

sections.title: Taqwa: Definition & Layers
sections.summary: Taqwa is guarding the heart from Allah’s displeasure by obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions.
bullets: Heart layer: sincerity (ikhlas), presence (hudur), reliance (tawakkul).
Action layer: fara’id on time, halal integrity, guarding gaze and tongue.
Social layer: trustworthiness, justice, compassion, fulfilling amanah.
Economic layer: avoid riba, honesty in trade, modest consumption.
Crisis layer: sabr + shukr under trials and blessings.

sections.title: The Taqwa Ladder
sections.summary: A practical scaffold from personal discipline to communal benefit and ummatic service.
bullets: Step 1: Personal—daily salat with presence, dhikr, Qur’an portion.
Step 2: Family—mercy at home, ties of kinship, shared learning.
Step 3: Community—masjid life, volunteering, local relief.
Step 4: Ummah & Humanity—projects that spread knowledge, justice, mercy.
Each higher step presumes the stability of the lower.

sections.title: Digital Shields & Clean Timer
sections.summary: Guard the gates: design digital kalkanlar (shields) and run a clean-time counter with mercy-based resets.
bullets: App/website block lists aligned with your known triggers.
Phone-free hours (post-Isha to post-Fajr) for sleep and dawn light.
Public commitment with a trusted buddy; immediate tawbah protocol.
Replace: walking, wudu’, dhikr beads, reading circles.
Metrics: ‘clean days’, ‘urges resisted’, ‘service acts after lapses’.
practices: 3–7–30–90 day clean milestones with sadaqah pledges.
Zikir micro-sets (e.g., after each urge: 10× istighfar + 1 good deed).

sections.title: Taqwa Index (TE) — Spec & Weights
sections.summary: A transparent, mercy-centered index to track practices without breeding pride; private by default.
bullets: Foundations carry multipliers: obligatory on time ×2; halal income ×1.5; gaze/ tongue guard ×1.2.
Istikrar bonus: weekly consistency +10%; clean-timer milestones add one-off boosts.
Tawbah-boost: lapses followed by repair acts apply a recovery coefficient.
Hidden mode: suppresses public badges to fight riya’.
Community weight caps: service points limited unless personal foundations are stable.
questions: How can I keep score privately yet stay motivated?

sections.title: Percentile Targets (Global Heuristics)
sections.summary: Approximate thresholds to visualize progress humbly; use as guideposts, not bragging rights.
bullets: >25%: all fara’id on time + daily Qur’an/dhikr habit + basic halal integrity.
>5%: + weekly charity/service + guarded gaze/tongue + weekly study circle.
>1%: + consistent dawn routine (Fajr jama‘ah when possible) + monthly community project.
~1-in-1,000,000: multi-year consistency across worship, ethics, and service with hidden mode and zero-riba livelihood.

sections.title: Ethics, Boundaries, and Adab
sections.summary: Seek Allah’s pleasure, not people’s gaze; keep creed safe; avoid sectarian harm.
bullets: No anthropomorphism, no negation; follow sound creed.
Avoid riya’: prefer hidden good; keep TE private by default.
Stay within madhhab boundaries in ibadah; consult scholars for nuance.
Disagree with adab; seek unity on essentials and mercy on details.
Protect dignity: no shaming, no exposure of faults.

sections.title: Family, Work, and Society
sections.summary: Ma'rifah blossoms when it reforms daily roles: family mercy, honest work, trustworthy citizenship.
bullets: Home: gentleness, humor, shared worship and learning.
Work: amanah, excellence (ihsan), no riba/haram revenue.
Society: help the vulnerable; volunteer; be a bridge of mercy.
Digital citizenship: truthfulness, modesty, no harm (la darar).
Seasonal rhythms: Ramadan, Dhul-Hijjah, retreats, sadaqah plans.

sections.title: Daily/Weekly Program
sections.summary: Minimal, sustainable program to internalize one Name at a time.
bullets: Daily: one Name—read meaning, reflect 5–10 min, live one action.
After each prayer: short dhikr set + gratitude note.
Weekly: attend a circle; review notes; one charity or help act.
Monthly: mini-retreat (half day) + digital detox window.
Quarterly: reassess goals; re-balance the Ladder steps.
practices: Attach reflection to fixed cues (post-prayer, commute).
Use clean timer + shields; pair slips with immediate repair.

sections.title: Glossary of Core Terms
sections.summary: Quick meanings for the spiritual vocabulary used throughout.
bullets: Ma'rifah: heart-knowledge of Allah that transforms worship.
Ihsan: worship Allah as if you see Him; if not, know He sees you.
Taqwa: guarding oneself from Allah’s displeasure.
Tawbah: sincere return with regret, abandonment, resolve, repair.
Fitrah: innate disposition oriented to truth and goodness.

sections.title: Method & Bibliography (Condensed)
sections.summary: Texts, methods, and disciplines we cross-wove, with humility about limits.
bullets: Method: text analysis (Qur’an/hadith), classical commentaries, comparative ethics, habit science, sociology of religion.
Primary: Qur’an; Sahih hadith; Ghazali (Ihya’), Nawawi, Ibn al-Qayyim.
Secondary: habit formation, attention science, meaning-in-life research; selected cosmology/philosophy of religion texts.
Limitations: cultural variance, measurement bias, riya’ risk—thus privacy-first metrics.
Ethic: mercy, dignity, gradualism; no exposure of private struggles.
refs: Al-Ghazali, Ihya’; Al-Nawawi, Riyad al-Salihin; Ibn al-Qayyim, Madarij.
Contemporary works on habits, attention, awe (general).
